title: Share Trading Policy

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Includes the Chairman. Dealing decisions during a blackout period are made by the Chairman (for other Directors) or the Audit Committee Chairman (for the Chairman), in each case in their sole discretion and notified to the Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Senior Managers
tiers.description: Managers who regularly report to the Board and attend Board meetings; individually notified and advised of the policy. Must advise the Company Secretary of trading outside blackout periods; blackout-period dealing is decided by the Chief Executive Officer in their sole discretion.

tiers.name: Other Employees
tiers.description: No advice is required for trading outside blackout periods; blackout-period dealing is decided by the Chief Executive Officer, as for Senior Managers.

windows.end_anchor: the date of announcement of the full year results
the date of announcement of the half-year results

rules.detail: The Policy has no definition of 'dealing' and never refers to derivatives, options over shares (other than the company's own incentive scheme options), or any other financial product.
No hedging concept, defined term or prohibition appears anywhere in the Policy.
Not referred to; the Policy contains no restriction on financing arrangements of any kind.
Granting security or a charge over shares is not referred to.
No holding period, intention test or short-term trading restriction is stated beyond the two blackout periods.

clearance.approver: Chairman (for Directors other than the Chairman)
clearance.evidence: Dealings inside a blackout period are to be decided for Directors (other than the Chairman) by the Chairman ... in their sole discretion and in each case notified to the Company Secretary. Any prior written clearance to trade in Exceptional Circumstances must specify the duration of such clearance and must be in writing.
for the Chairman by the Audit Committee Chairman ... in their sole discretion and in each case notified to the Company Secretary.

clearance.approver: Chief Executive Officer (blackout-period dealing); Company Secretary (advice of dealing outside a blackout period)
clearance.evidence: Dealings inside a blackout period are to be decided ... for the Senior Managers and Other Employees by the Chief Executive Officer in each case in their sole discretion and in each case notified to the Company Secretary.
Other Employees: No advice required [outside a blackout period]. Dealings inside a blackout period are to be decided ... for the Senior Managers and Other Employees by the Chief Executive Officer.

exceptions.approver: Chairman, Audit Committee Chairman or Chief Executive Officer, per Guideline 4
exceptions.evidence: Directors, Senior Managers and Other Employees should not deal in Macquarie Telecom shares during a blackout period unless Exceptional Circumstances exist. Exceptional Circumstances means severe financial hardships or other circumstances considered to be exceptional.

exceptions.approver: Chairman, Audit Committee Chairman or Chief Executive Officer, per Guideline 4
exceptions.evidence: Exceptional Circumstances means ... including a court order or court enforceable undertakings in a bona fide family settlement to transfer Macquarie Telecom shares or some other overriding legal or regulatory requirements to transfer Macquarie Telecom shares.

The issue of shares or the grant or exercise of options under share incentive schemes is not deemed to be dealing in Macquarie Telecom shares. The subsequent sale of shares is, however, a dealing which is subject to this policy.

exemption_authority: No general Board waiver power is stated. The only relief from a blackout-period restriction is the Exceptional Circumstances test in Guideline 3, decided in the sole discretion of the applicable Appropriate Officer under Guideline 4 (Chairman, Audit Committee Chairman, or Chief Executive Officer).

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy never defines 'Dealing' or 'dealing in shares' and contains no reference to derivatives, hedging, margin lending, secured financing or encumbrance of any kind.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: As drafted, the Policy does not itself restrict entering an OTC collar or a loan secured on Macquarie Telecom shares; the only textual constraints are the two blackout windows and general insider trading law if an actual sale or transfer of the shares is involved.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The issue of shares or the grant or exercise of options under share incentive schemes is not deemed to be dealing in Macquarie Telecom shares. The subsequent sale of shares is, however, a dealing which is subject to this policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Vesting and exercise of incentive plan securities is free of the Policy, but any subsequent sale (e.g. to fund a collar premium, or on settlement) is a dealing subject to blackout timing and the notification/approval regime.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Exceptional Circumstances means severe financial hardships or other circumstances considered to be exceptional, including a court order or court enforceable undertakings in a bona fide family settlement to transfer Macquarie Telecom shares or some other overriding legal or regulatory requirements to transfer Macquarie Telecom shares.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Provides a narrow gateway for a forced or lender-driven sale of the collared shares to proceed during a blackout period, at the sole discretion of the relevant Appropriate Officer.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Attached is the Macquarie Telecom Group Limited Share Trading Policy, which is provided so as to comply with ASX Listing Rule 12.9 when it comes into effect on 1 January 2011.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is a very old (2010), minimal document; given its silence on derivatives, hedging and secured financing (all now standard in modern ASX policies), the bank should confirm this is still the company's current lodged policy before relying on its silence.

summary: This is a short, 2010-era policy that never defines 'dealing' and contains no provisions at all on derivatives, hedging, monetisation, short selling, stock lending, CFDs, margin lending, encumbrance or secured financing. On its face, neither the purchased put and written call nor a loan secured on the collared shares is prohibited by the Policy's express terms. The shares themselves remain subject to two annual blackout periods (1 July to full-year results, and 1 January to half-year results) for any actual sale or transfer needed to establish, unwind or settle the structure, during which Directors, Senior Managers and Other Employees need sole-discretion clearance from the Chairman, Audit Committee Chairman or CEO respectively (or can rely on the narrow Exceptional Circumstances hardship/court-order gateway); outside a blackout period, Directors and Senior Managers must simply notify the appropriate officer, and Other Employees need not do even that. Given the document's age and narrow scope compared to modern ASX-listed company policies, the bank should confirm this remains the company's current lodged trading policy before relying on its silence on financing and hedging.
